text: Hiroshima. The sixth of August, nineteen forty-five.
A city of rivers and bridges, of trams and schools. The working day had just begun.
sub: A city of rivers and bridges, of trams and schools.|The working day had just begun.

text: At eight fifteen, an American B-29 bomber, the Enola Gay, released a single atomic bomb.
sub: At 8:15, an American B-29 bomber, the Enola Gay,|released a single atomic bomb.
asr: At 8.15, an American B-29 bomber, the Enola Gay, released a single atomic bomb.

text: It exploded about six hundred metres above the city. In an instant, the heart of Hiroshima was gone.
sub: It exploded about 600 metres above the city.|In an instant, the heart of Hiroshima was gone.
asr: It exploded about 600 meters above the city. In an instant, the heart of Hiroshima was gone.

text: In the months that followed, an estimated ninety thousand to a hundred and sixty-six thousand people died.
sub: In the months that followed, an estimated|90,000 to 166,000 people died.
asr: In the months that followed, an estimated 90,000 to a hundred and sixty-six thousand people died.

text: Three days later, clouds hid the city of Kokura, so a second bomber, Bocks-car, turned toward Nagasaki.
sub: Three days later, clouds hid the city of Kokura,|so a second bomber, Bockscar, turned toward Nagasaki.
asr: Three days later, clouds hid the city of Kokura, so a second bomber, boxgar, turned toward Nagasaki.

text: At eleven-oh-two, a plutonium bomb exploded over the Oorah-kahmi valley. Sixty to eighty thousand people died.
sub: At 11:02, a plutonium bomb exploded over the Urakami valley.|60,000 to 80,000 people died.
asr: At 11.02, a plutonium bomb exploded over the Ura-Kami Valley. 60 to 80,000 people died.

text: On the fifteenth of August, Japan announced its surrender. The war was over. For the survivors, the hibakusha, it was not.
sub: On 15 August, Japan announced its surrender. The war was over.|For the survivors, the hibakusha, it was not.
asr: On the 15th of August, Japan announced its surrender. The war was over. For the survivors, the Hibakusha, it was not.

text: Sadako Sasaki was two years old when the bomb fell on Hiroshima. At twelve, sick with leukemia, she folded paper cranes, hoping to live.
sub: Sadako Sasaki was 2 years old when the bomb fell on Hiroshima.|At 12, sick with leukemia, she folded paper cranes, hoping to live.

text: After she died, her classmates raised a monument to her, and to every child the bombs had taken.
sub: After she died, her classmates raised a monument to her,|and to every child the bombs had taken.

text: The next spring, in the ashes, the oleander bloomed.
sub: The next spring, in the ashes, the oleander bloomed.

text: Every year at eight fifteen, Hiroshima falls silent. And the survivors keep telling their story, so that it never happens again.
sub: Every year at 8:15, Hiroshima falls silent.|And the survivors keep telling their story, so that it never happens again.
asr: Every year at 815, Hiroshima falls silent, and the survivors keep telling their story so that it never happens again.
